newsitem.title: USA: Brent crude appeal to U.S. Gulf flounders further.
newsitem.headline: Brent crude appeal to U.S. Gulf flounders further.

text.p: Late North Sea Brent trading in the U.S. saw prices climb slightly, closing out a week of drastic losses for the market.
Traders confirmed a total of 500 lots were sold for March paper Brent at $21.05 a barrel, 3 cents higher than the IPE settlement price.
A Wall Street trader bought another 400 lots at the same $21.05 level, and then turned around and sold a 200 lot slice at $21.06.
Traders said the same Wall Street player bought two March/April Brent spreads, one at 34 cts and one at 35 cts.

Outright Brent prices faltered badly, in-line with drastic declines in NYMEX crude and products. March crude futures slid 87 cents to settle at $22.23 a barrel, and March IPE Brent ended 74 cts lower at $21.02 a barrel.
Technical triggers and sentiment the products in both London and New York were over overpriced pressured crude.
Forecasts for warmer temperatures in the U.S. heating oil belt along the Northeast corridor, and bearish gasoline fundamentals, played into the crude downturn, traders said.
Transatlantic arbitrage narrowed further, closing down most opportunities for bringing new cargoes to the U.S. Gulf in the immediate-term, traders said.
The spread between West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and Brent hovered around the $1.20-30 a barrel level, down 15 cts from Thursday, and some 40 cts from last week.
The lack of Brent on offer to the U.S. Gulf provoked a slight recovery in the Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James market.
Latin American developments saw Argentina's YPF sell two cargoes of Canadon Seco crude on Friday, moving two separate 380,000 barrel parcels at West Texas Intermediate -$2.47 FOB.
The first cargo is a February 23-24 loader, and the second a February 27-28, trade sources said.
Both cargoes were headed to Far East destinations.
